value.rationale: The Chvátal graph is a canonical extremal triangle-free four-regular four-chromatic graph. Its 12-versus-14 matching edge incidences create a structurally intelligible set of exactly 48 lowest-order lost Fourier modes. The full signed spectrum and sharp 5067/256 projection amplification quantify an identifiable measurement/recovery problem and cannot be inferred from the unsigned matching count or chromatic characterization. Exact finite recovery benchmarks and the graph-specific cancellation structure plausibly support comparisons across small dimer systems; no arbitrary slice or unproved infinite generalization is asserted.
